decision: A bare command name is resolved through the PATH the child will use, and the first executable match's directory must be a trusted binary directory or the call is refused. A name with no match at all is passed through (spawn reports ENOENT). An absolute argv0 keeps the pre-existing dir + realpath check. A raw command name found inside a trusted directory is passed through unchanged, so the exec'd string never changes for a trusted tool.
why: The module docstring claimed a realpath check a bare name never reached. Resolving through the trusted list closes the poisoned-PATH route; refusing every unmatched name would make a stub command (and the existing tsx journey) unrunnable for no gain, since no file can execute.
